newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan students protest against violent crime.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan students protest against violent crime.

text.p: About 40 Taiwan students demonstrated in front of the island's cabinet building on Monday to protest at the government's failure to check violent crime.
The students, angry at the recent kidnap and murder of the teenage daughter of a famous actress, demanded the resignation of Premier Lien Chan and a cabinet reshuffle.
"We want the cabinet of Lien Chan to step down to take responsibility for the fear that has been inflicted on the people, especially women," student leader Wen Chun-ya said in a statement.

Taiwanese were shocked by last week's discovery of the body of 17-year-old Pai Hsien-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping. Her kidnappers, who dumped her naked body in a river, have not been caught.

Shortly after the rally, a cabinet source said Lien planned to hold a cross-department meeting on Tuesday to address Taiwan's worsening crime problem in an effort to tackle public disenchantment towards the government.
"The heads of relevant departments would be invited to take part in the meeting to work out concrete measures to curb crimes," said the source, who declined to be identified.
The source said Lien was expected to make a policy statement in the meeting, which would mark the first comment by the premier since news of the murder broke a week ago.
Around 50,000 people demonstrated on Sunday and staged an all-night vigil outside Taipei's Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall in protest at the island's worsening crime levels.
President Lee Teng-hui on Friday apologised for "worsening social law and order" and said his government would take full responsibility.
